title: Ironhollow Rising Again
premise: Ada Blackwood survives in Ironhollow, a valley where magic cannot enter, by stealing memories and selling them to the desperate. When a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue, Ada discovers the girl carries a living memory of the war that magic was banished to end — and that the child's guardians, the Hollow Wardens, will burn the valley to reclaim it. Guided by her found family of misfit thieves, Ada must smuggle the child out while deciding whether to return the memory to the world. In the end, Ada gives up her own stolen hoard — including memories of her dead mother — to anchor the secret safely in many minds at once, breaking the Wardens' claim and choosing her makeshift family over the inheritance she never had.
about_author: Mirabel Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters never meant to be read, an obsession that seeps into every story she tells. She writes about thieves, orphans, and the things people carry because they cannot put them down.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet Ironhollow and Ada's trade: she lifts memories with a touch and sells them in vials to grieving townsfolk. A job goes wrong when a client recognizes his own stolen childhood. Emotional beat: establish Ada's cynicism and the loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On a rain-lashed night, a six-year-old girl appears at Ada's door, mute except for words in a language no one has spoken since the Sundering. The girl clutches a locket that hums against Ada's memory-stealing gift — and resists it. Emotional beat: wary wonder; Ada's armor cracks for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Locket Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with a flashback chapter from her mother's voice inside the locket. Touching the artifact floods Ada with fragments of the ancient war and proof that magic didn't die — it was imprisoned, and the valley is its lock. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Family You Steal
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts among Ada's crew: Bram the fence, Sefa the forger, old Tull the lockpick. They argue over what to do with the child, whom Sefa names Wren. Each reveals why they can't leave the valley. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under pressure.

chapters.title: Riders in Grey
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Hollow Wardens arrive in Ironhollow wearing borrowed faces, asking polite questions about a missing child. Bram lies badly and buys time with a bribe he can't afford. Emotional beat: the outside world's menace pressing in; survival has a price and it's rising.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Wardens take hostages from the town, including Tull, demanding the child by dawn. Ada proposes the unthinkable: use her stolen-memory hoard to forge a false trail out of the valley. Emotional beat: guilt, sacrifice, the crew choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: Tunnels Under the Lock
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered in simple, strange prose as she begins to speak Common. The crew flees through forgotten mine shafts where magic leaks like water, and Wren's language starts unlocking doors sealed since the Sundering. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the past is waking up.

chapters.title: The War That Never Ended
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ambushed at the valley's edge, Ada learns the truth: the Wardens aren't hunting Wren to destroy her but to use her blood to reopen the prison and finish their ancestors' war. Tull dies buying their escape. Emotional beat: grief and fury; Ada refuses to be anyone's weapon or pawn.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. At the prison-gate beneath Ironhollow, Ada touches the locket one last time and pours her entire stolen hoard — every memory she ever took, including her mother's face — into the lock, distributing the secret into thousands of sleeping minds so no single hand can hold it. The gate seals forever; the Wardens' claim shatters. Emotional beat: devastating, liberating sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ironhollow Rising Again
chapters.summary: Wren's POV closing into Ada's epilogue voice. Spring comes to the valley; magic returns gently now that the lock holds, and the town must learn to live with remembering. Ada, lighter and emptier than she's ever been, lets Wren and the crew fill the space. Emotional beat: quiet hope — family chosen, not inherited, is still inheritance enough.
